Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for issue #6834: phase-failure heal reports must carry a verified reporter identity

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `c5902a12a0cffef2ac8d97251f52e37f2b28b76e`, branch `main` (symbolic ref `main`). There is no integration-branch metadata, so there is no ref mismatch.

Automation surface (§20.E)
- No new script, workflow or supervisor. The change only edits existing code.
- Entry points are unchanged:
  - The `heal-report` job in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `plan.yml` and `implement.yml`, which runs when the phase job fails.
  - The `repository_dispatch` intake (`workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml` → `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`).
- No DB work, and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends verify_report_identity
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for exactly three things: grant `id-token: write` to the three `heal-report` jobs, remove the `phase_failure` exemption in the intake, and update the tests and docs. Everything needed already exists:
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh` (lines 165-180) already requests an OIDC token with `request-report-identity` and attaches it when the job is allowed to.
- `verify_report_identity` in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` already accepts `phase_failure`. `REPORT_IDENTITY_WORKFLOW_BY_KIND["phase_failure"]` maps it to `clarify.yml`, `plan.yml` and `implement.yml`, so `job_workflow_ref` binds the token to this repo's reusable phase workflows.
- Every caller already grants `id-token: write` at workflow level: `workflow-templates/ai-{clarify,plan,implement}.yml` and `.github/workflows/internal-{clarify,plan,implement}.yml`.

So no Python logic changes. The cheapest complete option is also the requested one; Boil the Lake does not widen the scope. I add one small regression assertion: every caller of the three reusable workflows must grant `id-token: write`. A missing caller grant would cause a startup failure of the whole phase workflow, so this assertion protects correctness (§6). It is well under 30 LOC.

---

1. Files likely to change

files_touched:
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml
- .github/workflows/plan.yml
- .github/workflows/implement.yml
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py
- README.md
- agents.md
- changelog.d/6834-phase-heal-report-identity.md (new)

The automation-path grant guard requires every staged `.github/` and `scripts/` path to appear exactly in `files_touched`. All of them are listed above. The issue was filed by the pipeline account (activation verifier), which counts as a trusted author.

2. Functions / modules to change

a. `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` (line 1665), `plan.yml` (line 2357), `implement.yml` (line 6109), job `heal-report`:
- Replace `permissions: {}` with:
  ```
  permissions:
    id-token: write
  ```
  Use 2-space YAML. A job-level block sets every other scope to `none`, so the job keeps no `GITHUB_TOKEN` scopes; `GH_PAT` still does the work.
- Update the job's comment block. Replace "`permissions: {}` keeps the job inside any caller's grant" with something like: "only `id-token: write` (granted by every caller wrapper) so the reporter can attach the OIDC report identity the heal intake verifies; GH_PAT does the work."
- Leave `needs`, `if`, `env` and steps unchanged.
- After editing, check `wc -c .github/workflows/implement.yml` stays under 480,000 bytes (§24). The change adds about 20 bytes.

b. `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`, the `*)` branch of the `REPORT_IDENTITY_STATE` case (about lines 285-293):
- Delete the `phase_failure` comment block.
- Change the condition to `if [ "${REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH}" = "true" ]; then _report_auth_reject "unauthenticated_report"; fi`. The `&& [ "${SOURCE_KIND}" != "phase_failure" ]` clause goes away.
- `REPORT_AUTH="absent"` stays for the non-enforcing path.
- The header comment at about lines 230-238 already describes the uniform rule. Adjust it only if it mentions the exception.
- The `workflow_run` (`event`) and `workflow_dispatch` (`manual`) origins stay as they are. They are not `repository_dispatch` reports.

c. `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh`, comment at lines 164-169:
- Reword to: the `heal-report` job is granted `id-token: write`, so a token is normally attached; `identity=absent` now means the request failed or a caller withheld the grant.
- No logic change.

3. Data structures affected
None. The payload envelope (`client_payload.report_identity`), `REPORT_IDENTITY_WORKFLOW_BY_KIND` and the `PROVENANCE_BOUND_KINDS` / `PROVENANCE_KINDS` tuples stay the same. Phase reports still go through the provenance gate after verification: run repository, phase workflow path, failed phase job, and a trusted linking comment.

4. API / interface changes
- Behaviour change only when `WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH=true`. A `phase_failure` report with no `report_identity` is now rejected (`WORKFLOW_HEAL report_auth=rejected reason=unauthenticated_report ... kind=phase_failure`, Telegram WARNING, nothing filed). It used to be accepted.
- With the default `false`, a tokenless phase report is accepted exactly as today.
- A phase report that carries a token is verified, as it already was. The log gains `report_auth=verified`.
- No env var, log prefix, label or identifier is renamed or added.

4a. ## Decisions

### D1 — Grant only `id-token: write` at job level on `heal-report`
- Chosen: job-level `permissions: { id-token: write }` on each of the three `heal-report` jobs.
- Alternatives considered: a workflow-level `id-token: write` in the reusable workflows; keeping `permissions: {}` and leaving phase reports to the provenance gate alone.
- Why: the job-level grant is the smallest one that lets the existing reporter mint the token. All other `GITHUB_TOKEN` scopes stay `none`, and the grant stays within what every caller already gives, so the job cannot fail at startup. Keeping `{}` would leave the authentication gap the activation verifier reported.

### D2 — Remove the `phase_failure` exemption entirely, not conditionally
- Chosen: one rule. When enforcement is on, every `repository_dispatch` report without an identity is rejected.
- Alternatives considered: keep the exemption until a sync deadline; exempt only phase reports from repos whose wrapper pin predates the change.
- Why: the issue asks for uniform enforcement. Enforcement already defaults to `false`, which serves as the transition window for consumers still on older pins. A per-pin exception would add a new version-detection surface for no security gain.

4b. ## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries touched:
  - Reporter side: the `heal-report` job can now mint a GitHub OIDC token. It runs only trusted support scripts checked out from `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` at `SCRIPT_REF` (`persist-credentials: false`), never PR- or issue-controlled code. The reporter asks for audience `coding-workflows-heal-report`, writes the token to a 0600 file, removes it on exit, and never prints it. The existing tests pin this: `test_request_report_identity_uses_the_heal_audience_and_never_prints_the_token` and `test_report_script_attaches_report_identity_without_logging_it`.
  - Intake side: tokenless phase reports no longer bypass `WORKFLOW_HEAL_REQUIRE_REPORT_AUTH`. That closes a forged-dispatch path: anyone holding the shared `GH_PAT` could send a fake `phase_failure` report, and it was accepted under enforcement on provenance alone.
- Authorization: `verify_report_identity` checks the RS256 signature against GitHub's JWKS, the issuer, the audience, `iat` freshness, that `repository` equals `source_repo`, that `job_workflow_ref` starts with `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/.github/workflows/{clarify,plan,implement}.yml@`, and the reporter run URL. Then the provenance gate runs as before. No new endpoint.
- Abuse cases:
  1. A forged tokenless phase report under enforcement is now rejected before any binding read or log fetch.
  2. A token minted by some other workflow in the consumer repo fails `job_workflow_ref_mismatch`.
  3. A token replayed from an old run fails `identity_stale` or `reporter_run_mismatch`.
  4. Any job with `id-token: write` can mint tokens for other audiences too, such as the claude-pool-broker one. That risk is bounded because the job runs only trusted support code, and the broker binds its own claims.
- Secrets: no token or PAT is logged. No secret is added.

5. Risks and edge cases
- Startup failure if a caller does not grant `id-token: write`. A reusable-workflow job that asks for more than its caller allows makes the whole run fail at startup, which would kill clarify, plan or implement, not just the reporter. All six known callers grant it today. A consumer with a hand-edited wrapper that dropped it would break, and a new contract assertion (see 6) pins the grant for every caller in the repo. Consumers get the new reusable SHA together with the re-rendered wrapper through `update_workflows.yml`, so the pin and the template move together.
- Consumers on older pins keep sending tokenless phase reports. Those are accepted while enforcement is `false` (the default) and rejected once an operator sets it to `true`. Document this in README: only enable enforcement after consumers have synced.
- The OIDC request can fail transiently. The reporter logs `identity=absent reason=...` and dispatches without a token. Under enforcement that report is then dropped with a WARNING, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.
- Self-repo: `internal-*.yml` call the phase workflows `@main`. The token's `repository` is the self repo, so verification binds `source_repo == self_repo`. No conflict.
- Conflict-detection note: none. The issue's line numbers match the code (intake lines 283-292, clarify 1665, plan 2357, implement 6109), and its claim that the callers already grant `id-token: write` is confir
